title: invoke-parser-quirks-journal
content:
Context:
- Ad-hoc debugging notes for a recurring parsing failure when consumer code tries to deserialize tool/function-call responses from the hosted API.
- Repro environment: local node dev server -> proxied to hosted-staging by dev-auth.
- Error frequently observed under higher concurrency and when responses stream.

Symptoms observed (summary):
- consumer throws JSON.parse errors or KeyError for keys that were present in earlier logs.
- partial chunk arrives then next chunk contains opening brace again (looks like concatenated JSON objects without separators).
- in some runs the top-level 'arguments' field is a string-encoded JSON rather than object.

Chronological attempts / notes (timestamps local):
- 2025-11-03 09:10: quick repro: curl -> got "SyntaxError: Unexpected token u in JSON at position 0". Replayed with --raw, saw response body starting with 'data: ' streaming prefix (server-sent events).
- 2025-11-03 10:02: added debug proxy to log raw bytes. Found sequence: chunk1 = '{"name":"lookup","arguments":"{\"q\":\"foo\""', chunk2 = ',\"limit\":1}"}
' -> double-encoded arguments plus split mid-string.
- 2025-11-04 11:45: tested with non-streaming endpoint (polling) -> parsing ok. Suggests streaming assembly bug.
- 2025-11-05 14:30: ran load test (50 concurrent) -> increased rate of malformed top-level arrays: saw messages like '{"name":"toolA","arguments":{...}}{"name":"toolB","arguments":{...}}' i.e. back-to-back JSON objects with no newline or comma.

Commands tried (snippets):
- curl streaming: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true" --data @payload.json
- node client-debug.js (simple fetch + res.body.getReader) -> accumulated chunks then JSON.parse(buffer)
- python: requests with iter_lines(decode_unicode=False) -> tried to join lines, still hit double-encoded arguments

Representative failing response (raw captured):
---RAW START---
data: {"id":"req-12","type":"response","payload":{"name":"fetch_user","arguments":"{\"user_id\":\"u-123\",\"fields\":\"[\\\"email\\\",\\\"name\\\"]\"}"}}

data: {"id":"req-12","type":"tool_log","payload":{"stdout":"OK"}}
---RAW END---
Notes: the 'arguments' value is a JSON string where 'fields' is itself a stringified array. So nesting is inconsistent.

Errors seen in consumer logs:
- Exception: JSON.parse at index 0: Unexpected token d (consumers that try to parse the raw SSE lines as JSON without trimming 'data: ').
- KeyError: 'payload' (in JS code that assumed toJSON returned an object but received undefined because parse failed).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Producer (runtime) sometimes sends function-call payloads as stringified JSON for arguments when tool outputs are created programmatically (i.e., it does JSON.stringify twice). Race in serialization codepath under concurrency.
2) Streaming encoder adds 'data: ' SSE prefix; some client code assumes pure JSON and lumps the stream together without handling SSE framing.
3) Upstream batching merges multiple JSON objects into a single TCP send buffer without separators which downstream assemblers treat as one big JSON -> parse error.
4) A middle proxy (dev-auth) is re-encoding or touching Content-Type / Transfer-Encoding headers causing library to change behavior.

What I tried to fix client-side (workarounds):
- SSE-aware reader: strip leading 'data: ' per line, join lines with '
', parse each line individually. Reduced "Unexpected token d" but still saw double-encoded arguments.
- Tolerant JSON unwrapping: attempt JSON.parse; if result.arguments is string, attempt JSON.parse on that. Worked for many cases but brittle (performance + risk).
- Buffer boundary heuristics: treat stream as sequence of objects by detecting '}{' boundary and inserting comma, wrap with [ ... ] then JSON.parse. This worked for back-to-back objects but failed when '}{' appears inside a string.
- Defensive try/catch and fallback to regex extraction for the 'arguments' substring then JSON.parse it. Ugly but got tests passing in CI for now.

Server/runtime inspection notes (what to check next):
- Inspect runtime serialization path: function call -> build FunctionCall proto -> toJson(). Look for code path that may call JSON.stringify on args that are already string. Check commit history around streaming/batching module (PRs: runtime#2279, #2291).
- Check SSE encoder: are we duplicating 'data:' prefix per chunk or only per object? Should we be sending 'data: [json]

' vs streaming chunk with partial JSON?
- Confirm headers: Content-Type should be text/event-stream for SSE. If Content-Type application/json but streaming body with 'data: ' that's wrong and some client libraries will try to parse raw.

Small experiments to run (next):
- Instrument runtime with a toggle to send non-SSE pure JSON streaming with newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) to see whether client errors persist. Metrics to record: % of malformed args, concurrency level, size of chunk.
- Create a minimal Node SSE client that reads event by event (EventSource polyfill) instead of manual body reader. See if EventSource handles the assembly properly.
- Add extra logging in proxy to capture raw TCP frames for a single failing request (harder but ultimate).

Hypothesis tests results (quick wins):
- EventSource polyfill test (2025-11-07): eliminated the "Unexpected token d" but double-encoded arguments still seen in 30% of runs. Conclusion: SSE framing partly responsible but not entire cause.
- Tolerant unwrap (2025-11-08): added to client tests -> passing. But longer-term we should fix producer.

Potential fixes (server-side):
- Ensure arguments are always encoded as JSON objects in the function_call payload (never string). One-liner: avoid JSON.stringify on args if already an object. Add assertion in serialization: typeof args === 'string' -> try JSON.parse to detect accidental stringify.
- For streaming: emit one complete object per SSE 'data:' event. Guarantee event boundary = object boundary. Avoid sending partial objects across events.
- Add newline or explicit separator between objects when batching multiple events into single send.

Open TODOs / Next actions (who):
- [Maya] add unit test to runtime serialization: simulate args as object and as string and assert final payload args is object (due 2025-11-12).
- [Ethan] audit PRs #2279 and #2291 for potential double-stringify (due 2025-11-11).
- [Priya] add integration test that uses EventSource polyfill across streaming path and asserts JSON shape (due 2025-11-14).
- Request: ops to capture tcpdump of a failing session (cc @infra).

Notes to self / random observations:
- This kind of bug has historically been a mismatch between code paths used in synchronous tool invocation vs async streaming tool logs (see INF-2127 from last year). Might be recurring pattern.
- Keep client tolerant for now (unwrap stringified args) but mark as tech debt.

Quick snippets for reproducer (save as repro/repro-node-stream.js) :
- minimal Node fetch + EventSource polyfill iterator to log each event and try JSON.parse(event.data).
- include toggles: useEventSource=true, allowDoubleEncodedUnwrap=true.

End state: durable workaround in client; server fix planned. This doc is scratch — keep iteration notes here.

Recent changelog refs (related PRs):
- runtime: PR #2291 (2025-10-28) changed streaming buffer flush behaviour (possible cause).
- console: PR #2155 (2025-09-14) added new debug headers that the proxy might forward.

If I forget: check both SSE framing AND double-serialize in the path where tool response is built from internal tool runner.

-- Maya
